clue.text: Actress taking lead aboard explosive vessel

parts.note: HE is short for high explosive
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: An actress steps aboard a ship loaded with explosives to play the lead role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' reads as a starring role but is the metal; it follows the explosive, as if aboard it, before the vessel is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Audrey and Katharine Hepburn were both famous film stars, so the surname is an example of an actress.

clue.text: For this person, more difficult to keep nothing

definitions.text: For this person, more difficult to keep nothing

indicators.note: to keep means to hold, so the comparative wraps around the nothing

parts.note: harder means more difficult
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Some people find it especially hard to keep nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the person: for them, keeping nothing is hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarder compulsively stores things and cannot bear to throw anything away.

clue.text: Lunatic went on Eurostar perhaps for continent early

parts.note: potty is British slang for crazy
the Eurostar is a train, so travelling on it is to train

explanation.surface: A madman takes the Eurostar to the Continent early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continent' suggests mainland Europe after Eurostar, but here it means able to control the bladder.
explanation.definitionFit: A potty-trained toddler has learned to use a potty, so has become continent at a young age.

clue.text: From this, milk shake Jack leaves

indicators.note: leaves means departs, so the card letter goes away

parts.note: to judder is to shake violently
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

explanation.surface: A milkshake recipe instruction: shake the milk, Jack, then leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milk shake' looks like the drink, but the words split: milk belongs to the definition and shake to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows are milked from the udder, the bag-like gland that holds milk.

clue.text: Poet and blundering scribbler

indicators.note: blundering means stumbling about clumsily, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: these seven letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet and a clumsy hack who scribbles words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scribbler' seems to describe a bad writer, but it is a thing written in.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribbler is an informal name for a jotter or pad of paper used for notes.

clue.text: Old relative in tank going from place to place

indicators.note: in places the relative inside the word for the tank

parts.note: a vat is a large tank for liquids
a gran is a grandmother, an older relative

explanation.surface: An elderly relative in a tank travels about the place, like a military outing.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant is a wanderer with no settled home, roaming from one place to another.

clue.text: Nero's sex position 500 came to see?

parts.note: sex is Latin for six, the Roman numeral VI, as Nero would say
a site is a position or location
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A saucy question about Nero's sex life and a numbered position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sex' is the Latin word for six, so a Roman emperor's version of it is VI.
explanation.definitionFit: To visit someone is to go to see them, so visited means came to see.

clue.text: Be independent — too genial potentially

indicators.note: potentially means the letters could become something else when rearranged

parts.note: these nine letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who is too friendly might find it hard to be self-reliant.
explanation.definitionFit: To go it alone is an idiom for acting on one's own without help.

clue.text: Missing persons?

parts.note: surface reading: people who have vanished, the subject of a police search
setter's reading: people who are simply not present, such as those off work or school

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase suggests a police case, but it just means people who did not turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are absent from where they should be, such as a class or workplace, are missing from it.

clue.text: Time to study the French foot pedal

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to read a subject is to study it at university
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Time to learn about the French word for a foot pedal.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a lever worked by the foot to drive a machine such as a sewing machine.

clue.text: Workers to die, suffering inside? Remedies needed!

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, so the letters of to die get distorted
inside places the jumbled letters within the workers

parts.note: worker ants are the classic crossword workers
these five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Workers are dying and suffering inside, so remedies are urgently called for.
explanation.definitionFit: Antidotes are substances that counteract poisons, so they are remedies.

clue.text: Lives with girl: shares maybe?
Outing Democrat — one in restructured party

indicators.note: restructured means rebuilt in a new form, so the letters of party are rearranged

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Democrat

indicators.note: in places the one inside the reworked letters

parts.note: these letters rearranged
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Democrat is outed while a reorganised party has one person within it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outing' reads as exposing someone, but here it is a short excursion.
explanation.definitionFit: A day trip is an excursion there and back in a single day, a kind of outing.

clue.text: See 2
Acknowledged grass should cover small garden feature

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so the grass goes either side

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
S is the abbreviation for small
a pond is a typical garden feature

explanation.surface: Someone concedes that grass ought to grow over a little garden pond.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond to a message is to answer it, which is to acknowledge it.

clue.text: Horse carrying large, unusual percussion item

indicators.note: carrying means the horse holds the abbreviation within it

parts.note: a steed is a horse
L is the abbreviation for large
rum is British slang for odd or unusual

explanation.surface: A horse bears a large, odd percussion instrument on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel drum is a Caribbean percussion instrument made from an oil barrel.

clue.text: Grey whales perhaps having traditional ideas?

parts.note: grey hair suggests being old
a school is a group of whales or fish

explanation.surface: Wondering whether grey whales hold traditional views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grey whales' reads as the species, but splits into two separate words.
explanation.definitionFit: Old school describes someone conservative or old-fashioned in outlook.

clue.text: Is it extra stout brought in to be selected?

indicators.note: brought in suggests the answer is carried inside the following words

parts.note: the letters straddle the three words

explanation.surface: A pub question: is this extra stout the one brought in to be chosen?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' suggests the beer, but extra stout here means very fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese describes someone extremely overweight, far beyond merely stout or plump.

clue.text: Article seen with crisis on the horizon

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
things come to a head at a crisis point

explanation.surface: A news article warns of a looming crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ahead lies in the future, coming up soon, as if visible on the horizon.

clue.text: As seen at the start in revised Racine

indicators.note: revised means altered, so the playwright's name is rearranged
in places the selected letter inside the rearrangement

parts.note: the playwright's name rearranged

indicators.note: at the start points to the opening letter of seen

parts.note: the first letter of seen

explanation.surface: A line seen in a revised version of a play by Racine, the French dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' looks like a little conjunction but is the chemical symbol, and it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the chemical symbol for the element arsenic.

clue.text: Comprehensive: where one learns poem shortened by a line

indicators.note: shortened means cut down, so the poem loses its last letter

parts.note: a uni, or university, is a place of learning
a verse is a poem
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A comprehensive school is where pupils learn a poem trimmed by one line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comprehensive' suggests the British state school, but it means all-embracing.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal means applying to everyone and everything, so all-inclusive or comprehensive.

clue.text: Nervous — too drunk to go to bed?

parts.note: anyone who has not gone to bed is still up
tight is informal for drunk

explanation.surface: An anxious person is too drunk to make it to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Someone too drunk to go to bed is still up and tight, which read together give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Uptight means tense and anxious, so nervous.

clue.text: I'm singer Justin, dropping an E for supper?

indicators.note: dropping means letting go, so one of the singer's vowels is lost

parts.note: taken as written
Justin Bieber is a pop singer

explanation.surface: Justin Bieber introduces himself, dropping a letter before supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supper' looks like the evening meal, but here it is one who sups, a drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbiber is someone who drinks, and to sup is to drink, so a supper is a drinker.

clue.text: Dead right leg — not right now?

parts.note: the late someone is someone dead
R is the abbreviation for right
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A dead right leg means something can only happen in due course.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the half of the field behind the batsman's legs is the leg or on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Later on means at some future time, so not immediately.

clue.text: Petition thus allowable

parts.note: so means thus
licit means lawful or allowable

explanation.surface: A petition is therefore permitted.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit is to ask for something earnestly, as one does when petitioning.

clue.text: Welsh lad around clubs avoiding booze ban

indicators.note: around means the Welsh lad surrounds the clubs

parts.note: boyo is a Welsh word for a lad
C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards
TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: A Welsh lad hanging around clubs while staying off drink imposes a ban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booze ban' looks like one phrase, but ban stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A boycott is a refusal to deal with someone or something, a form of ban.

clue.text: Long time before noon

parts.note: a year is a period of time
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A long stretch of time before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' reads as an adjective for the time, but it is the verb meaning to crave.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to yearn for it, desire it deeply.

clue.text: Have advantage over United in scoreless game?

indicators.note: in places the club abbreviation within the drawn result

parts.note: a scoreless game ends nil-nil, written 0-0
Utd is the abbreviation for United in football club names

explanation.surface: A football team gains the upper hand in a goalless draw.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to surpass or do better than them.

clue.text: US agent from Bow in New Orleans initially

indicators.note: in places the bow inside those initial letters
initially takes the first letters of the city's two words

parts.note: the first letters of the city's name
a bow is curved like an arc

explanation.surface: An American agent comes from Bow, the London district, to New Orleans.
explanation.definitionFit: A narco is American slang for a narcotics agent, an officer who enforces drug laws.

clue.text: Girl at bar ordered port

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: these nine letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl at a bar orders a glass of port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the fortified wine one might order at a bar; it is a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibraltar is a British territory with a major harbour at the mouth of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Kept appointment with fate in legendary town

parts.note: to keep an appointment is to come as arranged
one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: Someone met their destiny in a town of legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot is the castle and court of King Arthur in Arthurian legend.

clue.text: Manage Ulster county in need of regeneration?

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ulster

explanation.surface: Someone manages a Northern Irish county that badly needs renewal.
explanation.definitionFit: A run-down area is dilapidated and neglected, the kind of place earmarked for regeneration.
